text:
The wheel of the <term>Dharma</term> <gloss>the Buddha's teachings</gloss> of discipline is turned. It is appropriate here to be a holder of this wheel. His speech is excellent and pleasing to the mind, and he has forever abandoned the ways of ordinary, childish beings. His speech is pleasing, excellent, sweet to the ear, and harmonious with the joy it creates. It satisfies the mind and provides perfect bliss. The Buddha's speech is truly called "gentle." Through the special qualities of the <term>Tathagata</term> <gloss>Thus Gone One; a Buddha</gloss>, his power is such that it cannot be fully comprehended. His sons, who have entered the stages of realization, are ten in number and have transcended the world. Even you, the powerful lords of the gods, cannot fully know the excellent <term>Muni</term> <gloss>Sage; the Buddha</gloss> through worldly distinctions. Beings of the form and formless realms, those dwelling on the earth, the gods of the desire realm, and humans are all born from the mind. Among the accomplished <term>yogis</term> <gloss>spiritual practitioners</gloss> and all the distinguished ones in the world, the Leader of Men <note>the Buddha</note> is supreme. There is no sentient being who can fully know his greatness. The one who completely knows your greatness is the Buddha, known as the Gentle One. The name <term>Manjushri</term> <gloss>Gentle Glory</gloss> was bestowed upon you by the Victors of the past. This name was assigned to you by the Buddhas of the past, present, and future. By hearing your name within the assembly with a pure and one-pointed mind, without distraction, one attains knowledge and peace. May they reach the supreme, distinguished state of enlightenment at the end of existence. May all mantras without exception be accomplished, and for the birthplaces of wandering beings...

He entered <note>meditative absorption</note>. As soon as the Blessed One, Shakyamuni, entered into meditative equipoise, rays of light in colors of blue, yellow, white, crimson, and crystal emerged from the <term>urna</term> <gloss>the circle of hair between the eyebrows</gloss>. These rays illuminated this entire Buddha-field and other world systems. In an instant, all the planets and constellations were overwhelmed by this splendor and drawn in. Having been drawn in, they were restored to their respective places. Through the Buddha's blessing, they were gathered into that circle of the assembly and then disappeared back into the Blessed One's <term>urna</term>. Having been deprived of their light, all the planets, constellations, and stars became distressed and fearful. They sought refuge in the Blessed One, Shakyamuni, and remained with palms pressed together. Thus, they repeatedly cast themselves down and fell upon the ground. Then, the Blessed One, Shakyamuni, for the sake of helping both the wise and those sentient beings with the minds of ordinary children, spoke to all the planets, constellations, and stars: "Friends, including the hosts of gods and men, listen! Sentient beings depend upon their various karmic actions in the world. Even the <term>vajra</term> <gloss>indestructible</gloss> body of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is fully accomplished, as are the many worlds of gods and <term>asuras</term> <gloss>demi-gods</gloss>..."

<summary>This page describes the qualities of the Buddha's speech and the greatness of Manjushri, followed by a scene where Shakyamuni Buddha emits light from his brow to subdue and then comfort the celestial bodies.</summary>
<keywords>Shakyamuni Buddha, Manjushri, Dharma Wheel, Urna, Light Rays, Planets and Constellations, Meditative Equipoise, Karma</keywords>
